items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: recording like the one that’s based on John Steinbeck’s book, “Sweet Thursday,” I remember them doing that in Boston.

ctx.x: I guess there’s that story about him and writing “Mood Indigo” in such short order.

Well you know a lot of those things come out, too, of what he is when there. Sort of they don’t do much rehearsing. The rehearsals, even when they’re trying to make a new recording like the one that’s based on John Steinbeck’s book, “Sweet Thursday,” I remember them doing that in Boston. And they were playing in the hotel. And he each night, they would have new bits of music to drop in the middle of the program, when there was rehearsal. But I remember there was a number that he was doing that piece, that’s where…
In your experience watching that band from night to night, I’ve heard that they weren’t real consistent in their performances — that they could be on and off at a moment’s notice.
